key_insight: Localized charge deficits can trigger sustained electroconvection at about two thirds of the linear instability threshold.
engineering_relevance: Electrohydrodynamic designs should account for finite-amplitude charge fluctuations that can initiate convection below linear stability limits.
method: Nonlinear non-modal optimization using the full electrohydrodynamic equations.
Direct–adjoint search for minimum triggering charge perturbations.
Direct numerical simulation checks and edge-state analysis.
evidence_signal: Minimum triggering perturbations rise from about 0.5% of injected charge near the linear threshold to 3% at two thirds of it, consistent with direct numerical simulations.
watch_item: Thresholds are specific to the modeled unipolar-injection system; experimental agreement is explanatory rather than directly validated in the abstract.
paper_title: Nonlinear non-modal stability and minimal perturbations in electroconvection driven by unipolar injection
